state: There are no external users of Can, and immutable runtime contracts matter more than source compatibility. Bun 1.4.2 executes the authored TypeScript. Oxlint 1.85.0 has 73 diagnostics when checking runtime/ and tools/runtime/ while omitting vendor files: 48 unused-variable, 11 no-new-array, 6 no-control-regex, 5 no-thenable, 2 no-useless-spread and 1 no-this-alias. The user wants a reliable cleanup plan only. Existing tests make malicious then getters on purpose. Array(n) may mean a sparse array or a sized result, control regexes may reject invalid input, and spreads may isolate mutable collections. Candidate policies: evaluate and fix per occurrence, switch rules off broadly, or convert every flagged expression mechanically. After the warnings are gone, the repository can apply Oxlint --deny-warnings. Native JS/Bun lowering and contract preservation remain mandatory.

resolution.instructions: What approach should the plan prescribe for warnings attached to intentional TypeScript behavior?

criteria.targeted: Review usage and observable behavior at each warning; delete truly unused names, express intended operations clearly, and allow only small explained line-level suppressions for irreducible test or validation constructs.
criteria.global_disable: Use global or directory-level rule deactivation to avoid individual review of repeated warnings.
criteria.mechanical: Make every line match the rule suggestion directly, without separate checks for holes, error-triggering properties, or copied collections.

gate.instructions: How should the team establish a lasting lint baseline after the requested cleanup?

criteria.finish_then_gate: First reach zero warnings and confirm focused plus broad Bun tests, then enforce --deny-warnings over the same authored paths.
criteria.gate_first: Install --deny-warnings before cleanup so checks remain failing throughout the remediation.
criteria.no_gate: Do not require clean lint output in future runs after this batch is addressed.
